title_en: China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd., Shanghai Qingpu Branch v. Shanghai Donghe Real Estate Co., Ltd. and Chen Siqi — dispute over guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. Where a developer colludes with a natural person to sign a fake pre-sale commercial housing sales contract for the purpose of fraudulently obtaining bank funds, and, using the name of the natural person, enters into a commercial housing mortgage loan contract with a bank so as to obtain bank loans, if the commercial housing sales contract is subsequently confirmed to be invalid in accordance with the law, the developer and the natural person shall jointly and severally bear the liability for repaying the bank loans.

full_text_en:
China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd. Shanghai Qingpu Branch v. Shanghai Donghe Real Estate Co., Ltd. and Chen Siqi — dispute over guarantee contract

Ruling Summary

1. Where a developer colludes with an individual to sign a fake预售 commercial housing sales contract for the purpose of obtaining bank funds, and uses the individual's name to sign a commercial housing mortgage loan contract with the bank to obtain a bank loan, after the commercial housing sales contract is confirmed invalid by law, the developer and the individual shall bear joint and several liability for repaying the bank's loan.

2. In a预售 commercial housing mortgage loan, although the bank and the borrower (home buyer) have made a mortgage advance registration of the预售 commercial housing, such advance registration does not grant the bank a real mortgage right. Instead, it serves as a preemptive and exclusive protection allowing the bank to establish a mortgage right over the house after it is built and delivered to the borrower. If the property right of the completed house is not registered under the borrower's name, the mortgage registration cannot be completed, and the bank cannot exercise the mortgage right over the预售 commercial housing.

Plaintiff: China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd. Shanghai Qingpu Branch, domiciled at Qingsong Road, Qingpu District, Shanghai.
Person in charge: Guan Yinxi, Branch Manager.

Defendant: Shanghai Donghe Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hexiang Road, Baihe Town, Qingpu District, Shanghai.
Legal representative: Tong Binbin, Chairman of the Company.

Defendant: Chen Siqi, female, Han ethnicity, 36 years old, residing at Sanmen Road, Shanghai.

The plaintiff, China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd. Shanghai Qingpu Branch (hereinafter referred to as "Everbright Bank"), instituted an action in the Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendant Shanghai Donghe Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Donghe Company") and the defendant Chen Siqi regarding a dispute over a guarantee contract.

The plaintiff Everbright Bank alleged: On August 29, 2007, it entered into a "Personal Loan Contract (Mortgage, Guarantee)" with the two defendants. The contract stipulated that the defendant Chen Siqi would borrow RMB 370,000 (all currency units below are RMB) from the plaintiff to purchase a house located at Room 102, No. 20, Lane 185, Heru Road, Qingpu District, Shanghai, and the defendant Donghe Company would assume joint and several liability. After the contract was signed, the plaintiff disbursed the loan as agreed. Since the house sale transaction between the two defendants had been confirmed invalid by an effective court judgment, the plaintiff requested the court to order: (1) the defendant Chen Siqi to pay the interest of RMB 7,843.86 from March 20, 2011 to June 20, 2011, and interest from June 21, 2011 until actual repayment (interest rate calculated as per the contract); (2) the defendant Donghe Company to jointly and severally repay the loan principal of RMB 354,852.26, pay the contractual interest and overdue interest of RMB 7,843.86 (tentatively calculated up to June 20, 2011), and interest from June 21, 2011 until actual repayment (interest rate calculated as per the contract); (3) the two defendants to pay the plaintiff's attorney's fees of RMB 15,000; and (4) the plaintiff to have priority right to be satisfied from the mortgaged property, with any shortfall to be jointly and severally paid by the two defendants.

The defendant Chen Siqi did not submit a defense.

The defendant Donghe Company argued: An effective court judgment had already confirmed that the "Pre-sale Commercial Housing Sales Contract" between it and the defendant Chen Siqi was invalid. Therefore, the disputed "Personal Loan Contract (Mortgage, Guarantee)" was also invalid, and Donghe Company should not bear guarantee liability. Moreover, Donghe Company had already returned the house purchase price to Chen Siqi and had no obligation to repay Everbright Bank. Donghe Company requested the court to reject all of Everbright Bank's claims against it.

The Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai found the following facts at first instance:

1. On August 29, 2007, the plaintiff Everbright Bank entered into a "Personal Loan Contract (Mortgage, Guarantee)" with the defendants Chen Siqi and Donghe Company. The contract stipulated that Chen Siqi would borrow RMB 370,000 from Everbright Bank for the purpose of purchasing a house. Chen Siqi provided the house located at Room 102, No. 20, Lane 185, Heru Road, Qingpu District, Shanghai as抵押 property, with the scope of guarantee including interest, attorney's fees, etc. The loan term was from September 12, 2007 to September 12, 2037, and repayment was to be made by equal monthly installments of principal and interest. Donghe Company affixed its seal as the guarantor on the contract. After the contract was signed, Everbright Bank and Chen Siqi completed the collateral registration procedures on September 12, 2007, and Everbright Bank disbursed the loan on the same day.

2. On December 28, 2010, the Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai accepted a dispute over a pre-sale commercial housing contract filed by Chen Siqi against Donghe Company. During the trial, Everbright Bank participated as a third party. In its judgment, the Qingpu District People's Court held that Chen Siqi and Donghe Company, by signing the pre-sale commercial housing sales contract in a lawful form, concealed the illegal purpose of Donghe Company obtaining a bank loan. This act harmed the interests of others, and thus the contract was invalid. Since the pre-sale commercial housing contract was confirmed invalid, the purpose of the loan contract could no longer be achieved, and the loan contract should also be rescinded. Accordingly, the Qingpu District People's Court rendered civil judgment (2011) Qing Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 79, declaring the contract invalid and ordering Chen Siqi to repay Everbright Bank the loan principal of RMB 355,672.35 and interest up to March 29, 2011. Chen Siqi appealed against the judgment, and the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered civil judgment (2011) Hu Er Zhong Min Er (Min) Zhong Zi No. 1370, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. Thereafter, Everbright Bank received RMB 820.09 as repayment of the loan.

3. The attorney's fees incurred by Everbright Bank for this first-instance litigation were RMB 5,000.

The Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai held at first instance:

The "Personal Loan Contract (Mortgage, Guarantee)" signed between the plaintiff Everbright Bank and the defendants Donghe Company and Chen Siqi was concluded on the basis of equality and voluntariness, reflected the true intentions of the parties, and was lawful and valid. Since the loan contract was rescinded by the judgment, and Chen Siqi had not fulfilled the repayment obligation under the effective judgment, Everbright Bank had the right to exercise the mortgage right as provided in the contract. Donghe Company, as the guarantor, should also bear corresponding guarantee liability. The attorney's fees paid by Everbright Bank for this case amounted to RMB 5,000. According to the contract, this amount should be paid by Chen Siqi, with Donghe Company bearing the guarantee liability. The other attorney's fees claimed by Everbright Bank were not expenses incurred in this case and therefore were not supported. Since Everbright Bank's credit right was secured by both a guarantee and property security, Donghe Company should bear guarantee liability for the portion of the credit not covered by the property security. Since the validity of the loan contract had already been determined, the guarantee contract was valid, and Donghe Company should still bear the guarantee liability. Chen Siqi, having been properly summoned but failing to appear in court without justifiable reasons, had waived its right of defense.

In conclusion, the Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai rendered judgment on May 30, 2012:

1. Chen Siqi shall pay to Everbright Bank the attorney's fees of RMB 5,000 within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect;

2. If Chen Siqi fails to perform the obligation to repay the loan principal of RMB 354,852.26 (interest after June 21, 2011 calculated in accordance with the contract) as determined by civil judgment (2011) Qing Min San (Min) Chu Zi No. 79 and the attorney's fees of RMB 5,000 as determined in item 1 of this judgment, Everbright Bank may either agree with the mortgagor Chen Siqi to convert the house located at Room 102, No. 20, Lane 185, Heru Road, Qingpu District, Shanghai into cash, or apply for priority satisfaction from the proceeds of auction or sale of such mortgaged property. After the conversion, auction, or sale of the mortgaged property, any portion of the proceeds exceeding the amount of the claim shall belong to the mortgagor Chen Siqi, and any shortfall shall be paid by Chen Siqi;

3. If the mortgaged property provided by Chen Siqi is insufficient to cover all debts, Donghe Company shall bear joint and several liability for the insufficient portion. After bearing the guarantee liability, Donghe Company has the right to seek recourse against Chen Siqi.

Both Everbright Bank and Donghe Company appealed against the first-instance judgment to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court.

The appellant Everbright Bank argued: 1. According to the loan contract, the attorney's fees incurred by the creditor in realizing the claim should be borne by the debtor, and the guarantor should bear the guarantee liability. 2. Everbright Bank was entitled to claim from the appellee Chen Siqi and Donghe Company the interest of RMB 7,843.86 from March 20, 2011 to June 20, 2011 due to overdue repayment. 3. Donghe Company, as the actual user of the loan, had committed a joint tort with Chen Siqi and should bear joint and several liability with Chen Siqi to Everbright Bank, and the principle of "property security first, personal guarantee second" should not apply. Everbright Bank requested the court of second instance to set aside items 1, 2, and 3 of the original judgment, grant its claims in the first instance, and order Chen Siqi and Donghe Company to bear the appeal costs.

The appellant Donghe Company argued: 1. The loan contract between the appellant Everbright Bank and the appellee Chen Siqi had been rescinded, so Donghe Company should not bear the guarantee liability. Moreover, Everbright Bank was not bona fide, and its mortgage right should not be protected. 2. The effective judgment had declared the pre-sale housing contract invalid, and the disputed house belonged to Donghe Company. 3. The attorney's fees paid by Everbright Bank should not be borne by Donghe Company. Donghe Company requested the court of second instance to: (1) set aside the original judgment, amend or remand for retrial, and reject Everbright Bank's claims against it; and (2) order Everbright Bank and Chen Siqi to bear the appeal costs.

The appellee Chen Siqi argued: 1. The appellant Everbright Bank's request for repayment was reasonable, and it acknowledged the interest claimed by Everbright Bank, but it was unable to repay. 2. The attorney's fees were not reasonable expenses and should not be borne by it. 3. The disputed house was purchased by it, and any portion of the proceeds from exercising the mortgage exceeding the claim should belong to it. Chen Siqi requested the court to dismiss Donghe Company's appeal.

Upon second instance trial, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

Additional facts found:

1. The appellant Everbright Bank and the appellee Chen Siqi completed the advance registration (mortgage on pre-purchased commercial housing) on September 12, 2007. The expression in the first instance regarding this was inaccurate and should be corrected.

2. The appellant Donghe Company voluntarily provided a阶段性 joint and several guarantee to the appellant Everbright Bank for all debts arising under the loan contract of the appellee Chen Siqi. If Chen Siqi failed to perform its repayment obligations under the contract, Donghe Company guaranteed that it would perform the repayment obligations to Everbright Bank. The guarantee period was from the date of signing the contract until the mortgagor effectively set up the mortgage over the mortgaged property and the relevant title certificate and documents for setting up the mortgage were delivered to the lender for formal custody.

3. The appellant Everbright Bank participated in the first and second instance trials of the dispute over the pre-sale commercial housing contract between the appellee Chen Siqi and the appellant Donghe Company, for which it incurred attorney's fees of RMB 10,000. It also incurred attorney's fees of RMB 5,000 for participating in this litigation.

4. As of June 20, 2011, the appellee Chen Siqi owed contractual interest and overdue interest totaling RMB 7,843.86, of which the contractual interest and overdue interest owed from March 30, 2011 to June 20, 2011 amounted to RMB 5,263.01.

The issues in dispute in the second instance were: (1) whether the appellant Everbright Bank could exercise the mortgage right over the property in question; (2) whether the appellant Donghe Company bore legal liability in this case; and (3) whether the interest, overdue interest, and attorney's fees claimed by Everbright Bank should be supported.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

1. Regarding the first issue: whether the appellant Everbright Bank could exercise the mortgage right over the property in question

The court of second instance held that the advance registration of mortgage on the disputed property had a different legal nature and effect from the registration of mortgage right. According to the Property Law of the People's Republic of China and other relevant laws and regulations, after advance registration, any disposal of the immovable property without the consent of the holder of the advance registration shall not have the effect of property rights. After advance registration, if the claim is extinguished or no application for registration is made within three months from the date when the immovable property registration can be made, the advance registration shall become invalid. That is, the advance registration of mortgage does not register an existing mortgage right, but rather a right to demand the creation of a mortgage right in the future, which has exclusive effect. Therefore, the appellant Everbright Bank, as the holder of the advance registration of mortgage over the disputed house, before completing the registration of the mortgage right, had the right to demand the registration of the mortgage right over the disputed house when the conditions for mortgage registration were met or the agreed period expired, and could exclusively oppose any disposal of the disputed house by others. However, it did not have an existing mortgage right over the disputed house. The first instance judgment's finding that Everbright Bank had the right to exercise the mortgage right was erroneous and should be corrected.

2. Regarding the second issue: whether the appellant Donghe Company bore legal liability in this case

The court of second instance held that, pursuant to Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, the main contract for which Donghe Company provided a阶段性 joint and several guarantee was the loan contract in dispute. Although the main contract had been rescinded, unless otherwise agreed in the guarantee contract between Donghe Company and Everbright Bank, the guarantor Donghe Company should still bear joint and several guarantee liability for the debtor's relevant civil liability. The essence of a阶段性 joint and several guarantee is that the real estate developer provides a guarantee for the borrower to the bank during the period (from the date of signing the loan contract until the mortgage is effectively established and the relevant title documents are delivered to the bank for custody), and also provides a guarantee for the bank's waiting process to obtain a secure house mortgage. Once the house mortgage is successfully established, the阶段性 guarantee's mission is completed, i.e., the end of the阶段性 guarantee period coincides with the time when the bank obtains the borrower's house mortgage. In this case, before the advance registration of mortgage was changed to the registration of mortgage right, due to the principle of numerus clausus of property rights, the appellant Everbright Bank's right to dispose of the mortgaged house and to be satisfied in priority was deficient in terms of the elements for exercise. That is, the condition for the expiration of the阶段性 joint and several guarantee provided by Donghe Company had not been met. Moreover, the failure to meet this condition was not caused by Everbright Bank, but by the malicious collusion between Donghe Company and the appellee Chen Siqi, who used the pre-sale commercial housing transaction as a disguise to achieve Donghe Company's financing purpose, thereby harming Everbright Bank's interests and endangering the safety of the bank loan. Chen Siqi and Donghe Company were clearly at fault. Therefore, Donghe Company should bear joint and several liability for all debts arising from Chen Siqi's loan contract. As for the rights and obligations between Donghe Company and Chen Siqi after Donghe Company bears joint and several liability, the parties may have separate agreements and may resolve them separately. The issue of recourse was not addressed in this case.

3. Regarding the third issue: whether the interest, overdue interest, and attorney's fees claimed by the appellant Everbright Bank should be supported

The court of second instance held that the interest claimed by the appellant Everbright Bank against the appellee Chen Siqi in this case overlapped in part with the period covered by the effective judgment in another case. Therefore, in this case, the overlapping portion of the interest claimed by Everbright Bank against Chen Siqi was not supported. The interest payable by Chen Siqi in this case should be calculated from March 30, 2011. As for the attorney's fees claimed by Everbright Bank, when it applied to participate as a third party in the proceedings of the other case, the attorney's fees incurred thereby could not be claimed in this case. As for the attorney's fees incurred as a result of the litigation of the guarantee contract in this case, the first instance court had already set forth the reasons for its support, and no error was found.

In summary, the first instance judgment contained errors and should be amended. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 20 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China and Items (1) and (2) of Article 153 and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment on October 26, 2012:

1. Affirm Item 1 of the civil judgment (2012) Qing Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi No. 457 rendered by the Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai;

2. Set aside Items 2 and 3 of the civil judgment (2012) Qing Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi No. 457 rendered by the Qingpu District People's Court of Shanghai;

3. The appellee Chen Siqi shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect, pay to the appellant China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd. Shanghai Qingpu Branch the contractual interest and overdue interest for the period from March 30, 2011 to June 20, 2011, totaling RMB 5,263.01, and the overdue interest from June 21, 2011 until actual full repayment (calculated at a rate of 30% above the contracted loan executing rate based on the principal of RMB 354,852.26);

4. The appellant Shanghai Donghe Real Estate Co., Ltd. shall jointly and severally pay the following amounts on behalf of the appellee Chen Siqi: the loan principal of RMB 354,852.26, the contractual interest and overdue interest up to June 20, 2011 totaling RMB 7,843.86, and the overdue interest from June 21, 2011 until actual full repayment (calculated at a rate of 30% above the contracted loan executing rate based on the principal of RMB 354,852.26);

5. The appellant Shanghai Donghe Real Estate Co., Ltd. shall bear joint and several liability for the payment obligation of Chen Siqi under Item 1 of this judgment;

6. Reject the other claims of the appellant China Everbright Bank Co., Ltd. Shanghai Qingpu Branch;

7. Reject the appeal of the appellant Shanghai Donghe Real Estate Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
